A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MCIF benchmark, with readable text, tables, figures, and appendices A–E. V1's unfinished analyses are explicit placeholders, allowing reliable comparison with v2's completed content.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations in Tables 2–3 and Appendix E, although it explicitly describes the results as intermediate and incomplete.

after.justification: V2 reports original evaluations of 23 models, alongside modality ablations and question-answering analyses in Figures 2–3 and additional appendix results.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction pipeline and fixed-versus-varied prompt design are retained. Neither version proposes a new model architecture or training algorithm. Revisions to baseline evaluation prompts concern experimental settings; disclosure of the mixed-prompt lists does not establish a new construction method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the ACL 2023 scientific-talk data: 21 core presentations, 100 summarization samples, 220 QA pairs, four languages, three modalities, and 13 tasks. Short/long contexts and fixed/mixed prompts already exist in v1. The completed evaluations and analyses use this retained coverage.

E2.justification: V2 retains the original 21 models and adds GPT-oss 20B and Gemini 2.5 Flash, with results in Table 2 and Tables 9–10. Gemini introduces a commercial API-based multimodal reference into v1's open-weight-only comparison, substantially broadening the comparator scope.

E3.justification: Appendices C–D revise fixed QA prompts to request concise answers and add an answer-only system instruction. Sections 5.2–5.3 introduce controlled modality comparisons and long-form MCIFmix QA stratification. The exact prompt variant for the modality analysis remains inconsistent: Section 5.2 says MCIFfix, whereas Figure 2 says MCIFmix.

E4.justification: V1's Sections 5.2–5.3 contain only 'Work in progress'. V2 supplies modality ablations in Figure 2 and QA breakdowns by question modality and source for Qwen3, Phi4-Multimodal, Qwen2.5-VL, and Ola in Figure 3. These substantially extend the existing fixed-versus-mixed prompt robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's language averages and question-category breakdowns do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Many retained scores are replaced: MCIFfix short-context DeSTA2 WER changes from 45.1 in v1 Table 2 to 54.0 in v2 Table 9; Gemma 3n changes from 93.7 to 35.1. V2 adds new-model scores, previously missing LLM summarization entries, and modality/QA findings. Changed prompting and internal table discrepancies preclude treating all revisions as controlled same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The descriptive task definitions remain unchanged. Neither version contains a theoretical development, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation. V2's explanation of rescaled BERTScore adds interpretation of an existing metric rather than new mathematics.

C1.justification: The central benchmark novelty and scope remain intact. V2's abstract, introduction, and conclusion explicitly foreground the 23-model study and add specific headline claims about weak speech-video integration, fine-grained QA, and long-form summarization, extending v1's broader claim of performance gaps.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new ablations as evidence of underused video information and ineffective modality integration, and the QA breakdowns as evidence of weak fine-grained retrieval. It also replaces v1's broadly uniform prompt-degradation narrative with task-dependent sensitivity, including generally stable QA and inconsistent summarization behavior.

D1.justification: Appendix C expands from fixed prompts to the full mixed-prompt pools. Appendix D newly specifies a 4096-new-token cap and GPT-oss checkpoint/version details, while dropping explicit greedy-decoding information. V2 supplies dataset, code, output, and annotation-guideline access information, although its release statements conflict with Appendix D's retained 'upon paper acceptance' wording.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for GPT-oss, Gemini, verbose translation outputs, and multilingual LLMs, and replaces the original COMET reference with COMET-22. Section 2 sharpens distinctions from VideoMME and MF2 while retaining the same central positioning around joint crosslingual, multimodal, long-form evaluation.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, benchmark exposition, and existing results discussion. It consolidates the experimental-settings subsections, moves the main-text model catalogue into the appendix, standardizes macro-task terminology, and adds ethics and reproducibility statements. The overall numbered-section and appendix outline remains recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 replaces two per-language main result tables with one color-shaded, language-averaged comparison, retaining updated per-language results in Appendix E and dropping the unrescaled duplicate tables. It adds two analysis figures, three mixed-prompt tables, and a prominent title-page logo. Existing benchmark graphics are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: V1 explicitly leaves essential analyses and LLM summarization results unfinished. V2 supplies these results, substantive modality and QA analyses, and the omitted mixed-prompt documentation, substantially strengthening evidence and reproducibility. Numerical reliability remains imperfect: Ola's long-context MCIFmix WER is 6.6 in Table 2 but 36.8 in Table 10. This and the Figure 2 protocol inconsistency limit exact comparisons, but do not outweigh completion of the previously missing core evaluation.
